quest.title: The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells
quest.description: A wooden cabin has come to a stop above the water. This rather familiar house may currently play host to a certain old acquaintance. Is he in trouble again? Head over to ascertain the situation...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x35000

talks.objective: Approach the wooden cabin on the ice

dialogues.speaker: Cryo Cabin
dialogues.text: I hear footsteps, traveler by the shore. Please, if you would, halt a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it's this house again. If Paimon remembers right, some guy who hasn't come out in three hundred years lives in here! That's how he introduced himself to us back then, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: I remember this voice. You saved me once before, good travelers, and it appears we meet again, as I thought we might.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will you be needing my help again?

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Pardon the inconvenience, but I do indeed require your assistance once more.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Please find a way to drag this cabin near the material required to reinforce it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Reinforcement materials... What would those be?

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Do you see the wooden boxes scattered across the water? Those boxes contain various materials that I have gathered during this period of my wanderings.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Yes, I have resolved to expand my habitation, my home on ice.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Travelers on the shore, you once said to me that gratitude should be expresseed face to face, that discourtesy not be done.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Ever since we last parted ways by the lake, I have contemplated this matter: Should I again need the aid of travelers, how should I properly show them my thanks?

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: To me, to set foot upon Snezhnayan soil is unthinkable. But should the shorebound travelers be willing to set foot upon my abode, then I should receive them in person and give them my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So that's the reason for the renovation?

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Indeed, Traveler. I believe my home presently unfit for visitors. It is too narrow, too shabby, not hospitable enough by half...

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: People would look upon it and think that our being forgotten was a mere inevitability. Why, this house would be evidence enough — the final symbol of a past kingdom, reduced to such ignominity.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: For the sake of what dignity remains to us, this expansion is necessary, lest others think that we decrepit spirits of yesteryear have lost any shred of decency.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: Alas, these wooden boxes have been, by my miscalculation, scattered in non-ideal locations.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: I cannot control the direction of my cabin, so I fear I must ask you to <color=cyan>pull it up next to these boxes</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Churkaturin
dialogues.text: My utmost gratitude I give you, shorebound traveler. I will remember the aid you have rendered.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once the renovations are complete, should we again meet, you may make yourself more than welcome in my abode.
